text.en: Eleven-year-old Sachin walked into a cricket camp full of strangers and had to prove he belonged there.

In this autobiographical prose piece, Sachin Tendulkar remembers how he began serious cricket. His brother Ajit took him, aged eleven, to Ramakant Achrekar Sir's summer camp at Shivaji Park. Nervous under so many watching eyes, Sachin batted badly and the coach thought he was too young. Ajit persuaded Sir to give him another chance; this time Sachin played more freely and was accepted.
The lesson shows that talent needs hard daily practice, a patient guide and a supportive family. The schedule was tough: long morning and evening sessions, an early bus, and only one set of cricket clothes that had to be washed and dried between sessions. Sachin never complained, because he loved the game.
As you read, note words about routine and effort such as camp, rigorous, nets, schedule and exhausted. The text is written in the first person and the past tense, which is typical of an autobiography.
